review.decision_difference: Choose B to validate evidence-backed shortlist value for one founder segment first, then test approval-first outreach only if the shortlist gate passes; A instead validates the broader X-only prospecting-to-draft loop in one stage.
review.rationale: B better isolates the foundational discovery-and-qualification mechanism before outreach introduces major confounders. Its bounded cohort, manual-search comparison, predefined thresholds, downstream-use measure, and repeat window create a clearer stop, pivot, or continue gate. A tests a valuable end-to-end loop, but combining shortlist quality and draft readiness makes failures harder to attribute and provides a less precise sequencing decision.

review.decision_difference: A determines whether merge-boundary enforcement creates recurring value before testing centralized policy authority; B prematurely bundles that workflow question with shared ownership and cross-repository authority. Evidence from A therefore gives a cleaner continue, pivot-to-identity, or stop decision and can justify sequencing B later.
review.rationale: A isolates the adoption mechanism—required merge-time enforcement versus optional local use—using existing mcp-policy capabilities in one qualified repository. Its bounded probe, normalized observations, explicit retention test, and branching decisions make rejection and interpretation unusually clear. B is relevant and testable, but simultaneously varies workflow placement, remote shared authority, durable ownership, and multi-repository coordination, so a failed pilot would reveal less about which assumption failed.

review.decision_difference: Choose B to test whether the existing gateway is a distinct, useful routing component behind adopter-owned controls; choose A only after evidence suggests gateway-native operational controls are necessary and an operator is prepared to own them.
review.rationale: B more directly addresses the required boundary decision without first adding gateway-native production controls. Its bounded, independently reproducible probe isolates the gateway's contribution, tests realistic failure semantics, and compares it with established alternatives. A has stronger low-level safety mechanisms, but implementing mandatory authentication and deadlines partially advances the production-control-layer boundary before establishing that adopters need it.
